name: Chen Jianxing
current_role: Shareholder associated with Wens Foodstuff Group (per Hurun listing); no current public role found
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2016-2021) as sharing a Wens Foodstuff fortune with Wen Xiaoqiong, one of the Wen family members named as actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (Guangdong pig and poultry producer). No public filings or press found naming a 陈建兴 in a Wens director or executive role.
interesting_fact: Wens grew from a 'seven households, eight shares' rural partnership in 1983 into a company with thousands of employee-shareholders, after introducing an all-employee shareholding scheme in 1986.
notes: Could not confirm identity or role from public sources; appears to be a passive family shareholder rather than an executive. Contact only via Wens corporate channels (website/IR). Very low public profile.

name: Colin T. Moran
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Abdiel Capital (Abdiel Capital Advisors, LP), New York
profile: Hedge fund manager who co-founded Abdiel Capital with Geoffrey Gentile in 2006 after stints at Goldman Sachs and as a partner at Chieftain Capital. Abdiel is a concentrated, long-term investor and long-time 10%+ holder of low-code software firm Appian (APPN); in 2025 it also took a ~12% stake in Rise Gold (RYES), which is reviving California's Idaho-Maryland gold mine.
interesting_fact: Abdiel has reported as a 10%+ owner of Appian for years, filing more than 40 amendments to its Schedule 13D on the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before running money he trained as a historian and lawyer: a summa cum laude B.A. in History and Economics from Duke, an MSt in Modern History from Oxford, and a law degree from Stanford Law School (Order of the Coif).
notes: Low-profile investor; no published personal or firm contact email found. Rise Gold stake per Form 3 (Oct 2025): https://www.secform4.com/filings/1424864/0001193125-25-261127.htm. Education details from MarketScreener aggregator; worth double-checking.

name: He Qiqiang
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Chant Group (Changqing Group, 002616.SZ), Zhongshan
profile: Co-founded Chant Group (长青集团) in Zhongshan in 1985 as a gas and heating appliance maker, listed it in Shenzhen in 2011, and from 2004 steered it into biomass combined heat-and-power and industrial-park district heating, where it ranks among China's largest operators. Still chairman; fortune shared with wife Guo Miaobo.
interesting_fact: Chant Group pivoted from gas stoves and heaters to burning crop and forestry residues instead of coal, and its installed biomass CHP capacity ranks among the largest of China's peers.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting his business in 1985 he was a factory workshop director earning about 100 yuan a month, and his early goal was simply to save 1 million yuan, since its ~5% interest would yield 4,000+ yuan a month (told at a 2023 Yabuli entrepreneurs' forum).
notes: Highly relevant to energy theme (biomass CHP). Active in the Yabuli China Entrepreneurs Forum, which may be a warm route. IR email is the board secretary's office.

name: Xing Jiaxing
current_role: Founder and former chairman of La Chapelle (拉夏贝尔); no current executive role found (resigned Feb 2020)
profile: Born 1972 in Pucheng, Fujian, he moved to Shanghai in 1994, began as a clothing sales agent and launched the La Chapelle womenswear brand, aiming to build a 'Chinese Zara'; it became the only Chinese apparel company dual-listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong (A+H). He stepped down as chairman in 2020 and no longer controls the company.
interesting_fact: During the 2003 SARS outbreak he bet against the downturn and ramped up production; when shoppers returned, deep discounting made La Chapelle a nationally known brand.
deep_cut_fact: He learned his trade at a clothing-design training school for just six months, then worked at a Fuzhou garment firm sewing clothes, staffing the counter and delivering goods by bicycle before becoming a business supervisor. He later built a 1,000-mu cherry-orchard leisure farm (樱园) in his home village of Yangdun, Xianyang town.
notes: Sensitive: lost control of La Chapelle in 2020 after his shares were judicially auctioned, and the company later faced bankruptcy proceedings. Avoid these topics. No current public contact route found; hometown agritourism project may be his current focus.

name: Wen Zhifen
current_role: Chairman, Wens Foodstuff Group (300498.SZ), Yunfu, Guangdong
profile: A member of the founding Wen family and a named actual controller of Wens, he rose from vice president to president and vice chairman/CEO before becoming chairman. Wens, a 1983 village chicken partnership, is now one of China's largest pig and poultry producers with 100bn+ yuan revenue; he calls modern farming a high-tech, R&D-driven industry.
interesting_fact: Under his chairmanship Wens crossed the 100-billion-yuan revenue mark, yet he has publicly said he does not want the company to 'run too fast'.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in animal husbandry at South China Agricultural University's animal science department, later earned a doctorate-level degree at Sun Yat-sen University, and has been named a National Model Worker and shared a National Science and Technology Progress Award (second class).
notes: Hurun lists the fortune shared with Sun Fen (also a named actual controller). IR email is the board secretary's office. Education/awards from a third-party profile (cnpp.cn) - verify before use.

name: Alan A. Ades
current_role: Director and 10%+ owner, Organogenesis Holdings (ORGO); co-founder and President/CEO of A & E Stores, Inc.
profile: New Jersey retail entrepreneur who co-founded A & E Stores with Albert Erani and has run it for decades; he also founded Rugby Realty Co. in 1980. The Ades and Erani families became long-term controlling investors in regenerative-medicine company Organogenesis (maker of Apligraf), where he has sat on the board since 2003 and served as chairman until 2023.
interesting_fact: A retail and real-estate family office ended up as the anchor shareholder of a Massachusetts biotech: the Ades and Erani families' long-term stake is the reason both families hold Organogenesis board seats.
deep_cut_fact: His A & E Stores holds the 'PAY HALF' trademark for off-price clothing, footwear and accessories retail (filed 1992); he studied at the University of Michigan and NYU School of Law before going into retail.
notes: Very private; no personal channels. Corporate route via Organogenesis IR/communications. Bio details (A&E since 1966, Rugby Realty 1980, UMich/NYU Law) per Organogenesis board page; MarketScreener gives 1973 for A&E, so dates are inconsistent. Organogenesis currently in a difficult stretch (2026 guidance cuts, FDA items) - avoid.

name: Lin Xinliang
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun China (2014-2018) as behind 'Kerui Steel Plate'
profile: Appears on the Hurun China Rich List 2014-2018 with wealth attributed to a steel-plate business, Kerui Steel Plate (科瑞钢板). Searches in Chinese (蔺新亮) and English found no public record of this person or company, so identity and current status could not be verified.
notes: Could not identify the company or person in public sources (possibly a private regional steel firm; name/company romanisation may differ). Dropped off Hurun after 2018. Not recommended as an outreach target without further local-language registry checks.

name: Lord Haughey
current_role: Chairman, City Facilities Management Holdings (City FM), Glasgow; Labour life peer in the House of Lords
profile: William 'Willie' Haughey (b. 1956, Gorbals, Glasgow) founded City Refrigeration with his wife Susan in 1985 using savings from working in Abu Dhabi. A 1997 Asda maintenance contract let them buy back control from 3i in 1999; the firm, rebranded City Facilities Management, now operates internationally. Knighted, OBE, and made a life peer in 2013; noted philanthropist.
interesting_fact: He backed the Entrepreneurial Spark start-up accelerator, hosting its Glasgow 'hatchery' inside his City Refrigeration headquarters.
deep_cut_fact: City's corporate HQ, Caledonia House in the Gorbals, stands virtually on the site of his demolished childhood home; he started the business with about GBP 70,000 saved while working in refrigeration and air-conditioning in Abu Dhabi.
notes: Rich List entry shared with Lady Haughey (co-founder). As a peer he can also be written to via the House of Lords. Prominent Glasgow philanthropist and football (Celtic) figure; generally media-friendly in Scottish press.

name: Zhang Bei
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Jinghui Electric (Shenzhen) Co. (since June 1992); co-actual controller and ~24.5% shareholder of Shenzhen Crastal Technology / Buydeem (300824.SZ)
profile: Shenzhen small-appliance entrepreneur who has run Jinghui Electric (晶辉电器), an appliance manufacturer, since 1992. Together with George Mohan Zhang (Buydeem's chairman/GM) he controls about 52.5% of Shenzhen Crastal Technology, which owns the Buydeem (北鼎) premium kitchen-appliance brand known for kettles and health pots and listed in Shenzhen in 2020.
interesting_fact: Crastal started as an OEM appliance maker and built its own consumer brand, Buydeem, now a recognisable premium kettle and kitchenware label in China.
notes: Low public profile; the public face of the company is George Mohan Zhang. Best route is Buydeem's board-secretary IR email. Role details from Buydeem 2025 annual report (section on actual controllers).

name: Liu Jian
current_role: Minority shareholder in Yinjiang Technology Group / Enjoyor (银江股份, 300020.SZ); no executive role found
profile: Listed by Hurun (2010-2015) as sharing a fortune with Wang Hui, founder-chairman figure of Hangzhou smart-transport and healthcare-IT company Enjoyor (Yinjiang). At the 2009 IPO, filings showed Liu (written 刘健) holding 6% of controlling shareholder Yinjiang Technology Group and about 1% of the listed company directly; she has no public operating role.
interesting_fact: At its 2009 IPO, Yinjiang's prospectus claimed 93% of Hangzhou's and 82% of Zhejiang's intelligent-traffic market.
notes: Hurun spells the name 刘剑; IPO coverage spells 刘健 and describes her as Wang Hui's wife. Passive family shareholder. Caution: in Dec 2025 the company (now ST Yinjiang) and Wang Hui faced a CSRC investigation over disclosures - not a good outreach target.

name: Lu Yuanjian
current_role: Co-actual controller of Fujian Yuanli Active Carbon (300174.SZ) with Wang Yan'an; no formal company post since Feb 2018
profile: Born 1950, a chemical engineer-manager from Nanping, Fujian, who led and chaired Yuanli Active Carbon, which grew from a ~500-tonne plant (1999) into China's largest wood-based activated-carbon maker. He left formal posts in 2018 but remains controlling shareholder and is subscribing shares in Yuanli's acquisition of silica maker Tongsheng.
interesting_fact: Yuanli's wood-based activated carbon output grew from about 500 tonnes when the plant was built in 1999 to nearly 100,000 tonnes, making it the largest such producer in China.
deep_cut_fact: Before Yuanli he was director of Nanping No. 2 Chemical Factory and GM/chief engineer of Nanping Jialian Chemical; he later chaired the Evonik Jialian precipitated-silica JV in Nanping and served as president of the Fujian Activated Carbon Industry Association.
notes: Hurun lists co-owner as 'Wang Yanan'; filings give 王延安 (Wang Yan'an), his wife and fellow actual controller. Activated carbon/silica has energy-storage angles (supercapacitor carbon). Private; route via board secretary IR email.

name: Zhang Qiaomin
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Longji Group / Shandong Longji Machinery (002363.SZ), Longkou; left the listed company's board in January 2023
profile: Born 1939 in Longkou, Shandong, he went from village accountant to running the Shandong Automotive No. 3 Pump Factory, which he built into Longji Group, a brake disc/drum maker; Longji Machinery listed in Shenzhen in 2010. He has stepped back; Zhang Haiyan is chairman and sole actual controller per the 2025 annual report.
interesting_fact: Longji grew out of a village enterprise in Longkou's Hongguang village into a listed brake-component exporter supplying overseas auto-parts markets.
deep_cut_fact: His career began as chief accountant and then deputy village committee secretary of Hongguang Village in Longkou before he became director of the Shandong Automotive No. 3 Pump Factory, the seed of Longji.
notes: Elderly (b. 1939) and retired from the listed company; could not confirm whether alive. No longer named as actual controller in the 2025 annual report. liujian@ is the board secretary's published address (not the Liu Jian in this lane). Bio from Lixinger (third-party aggregator of filings).

name: David Hood
current_role: Chairman, Multiflight Ltd (private aviation, Leeds Bradford Airport)
profile: Yorkshire technology entrepreneur (OBE) who founded Shipley-based Pace Micro Technology, the modem and later set-top-box maker he steered through the 1980s-90s to its 1996 flotation. In 1994 he founded Multiflight, a business-aviation company at Leeds Bradford Airport offering flight training, aircraft management, engineering and VIP handling, which he still chairs.
interesting_fact: He started Multiflight in 1994 after becoming an aviation enthusiast, qualifying as a helicopter pilot and buying a Dassault Falcon 900B business jet.
deep_cut_fact: Multiflight is an official distributor in the Safran Helicopter Engines network and absorbed Yorkshire Light Aircraft and the Yorkshire Flying Club at Leeds Bradford as part of a site redevelopment.
notes: His work email is listed on Multiflight's own About page alongside the team, so it is published by his company. Pace was sold to Arris in 2016; tech/hardware founder story suits the entrepreneurship angle.

name: Jeffrey C Lightcap
current_role: Senior Managing Director, HealthCor Partners Management and Healthcare Venture Partners; Director of Heartflow, Inc. (HTFL) since 2011
profile: Healthcare venture investor and former M&A banker (Salomon Brothers, Kidder Peabody, Merrill Lynch) who was a senior managing director at private-equity firm JLL Partners 1997-2006 before joining HealthCor Partners in 2007. HealthCor backed Heartflow, the AI-driven non-invasive coronary-artery imaging company, whose board he has sat on since 2011 and which IPO'd in August 2025.
interesting_fact: He has stayed on Heartflow's board for more than 13 years through its 2025 IPO, and bought a further ~$1 million of shares in the open market in December 2025.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training: he earned a B.E. in Mechanical Engineering at SUNY Stony Brook before an MBA from the University of Chicago and a career in Wall Street M&A.
notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. HealthCor Partners' website appeared offline at time of research. Also on boards of CareView Communications, RTI Surgical and KellBenx (per 2026 proxy).

name: Qiu Jibao
current_role: Founder and (at last report) chairman of Feiyue Group (China Feiyue Sewing Machinery Group), Taizhou, Zhejiang; current status not confirmed
profile: Taizhou-born entrepreneur (b. 1962) who founded Feiyue in 1986 and built it into one of China's largest private sewing-machine makers (computerised industrial/domestic sewing and embroidery machines, 30+ overseas offices, supplier to Singer). Deputy to the 11th National People's Congress from 2008. Feiyue was restructured in 2009.
interesting_fact: Feiyue set up a US subsidiary in Pomona, California in 1997 (later Chino) and built a network of over 1,500 American dealers.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economic management at the Zhejiang Institute of Technology (now Zhejiang University of Technology).
notes: Sensitive: Feiyue fell into financial crisis in 2008 and was restructured in 2009; avoid. Last on Hurun 2005-2007. Little recent public information; current role unverified. Not to be confused with the Feiyue sneaker brand.

name: Zhou Lingen
current_role: Individual top-10 shareholder (~1.8%) of Hundsun Technologies (600570.SH), Hangzhou; no current executive role found
profile: Hangzhou investor listed by Hurun (2020) for his stake in Hundsun Technologies, China's leading maker of trading and core-system software for brokerages, funds and banks (controlled since 2014 by Jack Ma's Zhejiang Rongxin). Filings show him holding ~1.77% (c. 34m shares), one of the largest individual holders.
interesting_fact: Hundsun, which began as Hangzhou Hundsun Software in the 1990s, is the back-office software backbone of much of China's securities industry; in 2014 Jack Ma's personal vehicle paid 3.3bn yuan for its parent, Hundsun Group.
notes: Shareholding per Hundsun filings (shareholder table, 2022-2024). Likely part of Hundsun's founding/early team but not verified from a public source. Very low profile; only corporate IR route found.

name: He Congzhen
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun China (2021) with wealth from Tsingshan
profile: Appears once on the Hurun China Rich List (2021) with wealth attributed to Tsingshan Holding Group, the Wenzhou-founded stainless steel and nickel giant led by Xiang Guangda. No public filing or press source naming 何从珍 as a Tsingshan shareholder or executive was found, so the role could not be verified.
interesting_fact: Tsingshan, founded in Wenzhou in 1988, became the world's largest stainless steel producer and a major nickel supplier via its Indonesian industrial parks.
notes: Identity unverified; probably a private shareholder in Tsingshan or a related entity. Relevant to the energy/materials theme (nickel for batteries), but no outreach route found.

name: Sun Xiurong
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun China (2016) with wealth from 'Paixin' (IT)
profile: Appears once on the Hurun China Rich List (2016) with an IT-sector fortune attributed to a company romanised as 'Paixin'. Chinese and English searches found no company or public record matching 孙秀荣 and Paixin, so identity and current role could not be verified.
notes: Could not identify the company (romanisation unclear) or person. Not recommended as an outreach target without a business-registry lookup.

name: Han Yuyu
current_role: Largest shareholder (~25.5%) and co-actual controller of Suzhou Shijia Technology (002796.SZ); holds no company post
profile: Co-controls Suzhou Shijia Technology (世嘉科技) with Wang Juan (chairman) and Han Huiming (director/GM); together they hold about 36.4%. Shijia began as a precision sheet-metal enclosure maker for elevators, medical and telecom equipment, and expanded via its Bofate subsidiary into 5G base-station RF filters and antennas. She holds no executive role.
interesting_fact: Shijia supplies precision box/enclosure systems for elevators and medical devices and, through its Bofate acquisition, mobile-communication RF components for 5G networks.
notes: Passive family shareholder; operating leaders are Wang Juan and Han Huiming. Holding per 2025 annual report (as at 31 Dec 2025). Route only via company IR.

name: Chen Xiumei
current_role: Co-actual controller and shareholder of Fujian Acetron New Materials (阿石创, 300706.SZ), Fuzhou
profile: Together with her husband Chen Qinzhong (chairman/GM), she is a controlling shareholder of Fujian Acetron New Materials, a ChiNext-listed (2017) maker of PVD sputtering targets and evaporation materials used to coat flat-panel displays, glass, optics and solar cells. She held about 11.5m shares as of Q1 2026; the founders sold part of their stake to a private fund in 2026.
interesting_fact: Acetron makes the sputtering targets used to deposit nanometre-thin films on display panels and solar cells, a niche long dominated by Japanese and US suppliers; it exports to Japan, the US, Germany and Korea.
notes: Hurun spells co-owner 'Chen Qinzhong'; filings use 陈钦忠. Public face is Chen Qinzhong. Solar/display coatings link to the energy theme. Route via securities-affairs IR email.
